prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (RDC; call sign Juniper) provides 24/7 EMS intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch/coordination, surge declaration and regional coverage picture under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain ownership/local policy. RDC records caller reports, incidents/priorities/rationales, assignments/status/location/movement, coverage, maintenance/access constraints, authorizations/selection reasons, routes/destinations/consultations, arrival/handover; updates incident after facility transfer; compares thresholds, response/coverage and route/destination effects. Surge operations begin when queue age, simultaneous high-priority calls or staffed-unit availability cross approved thresholds; RDC monitors continuously and declares level. Computer Aided Dispatch Console (CAD Console) checks locations; displays incident/priority/travel/availability/access/staging options, current surge level and field/facility constraints. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates unit position/status, retains time-stamped changes, presents matching units, approved destination and instructions. Radio Coordinator Mistral uses Regional Radio Network/talkgroups to send incident/assignment/hazard/route/destination instructions to Paramedic Crew, requires repeat-back/ack, supports en-route updates/retries/alerts, sends Coverage Gap Bulletin. Controlled handoff only after crew ack and dispatch-floor confirmation. Paramedic Crew reports statuses, conflicts/hazards/delays, staging/arrival, handover complete, acknowledges destination and requests renewed consultation if needed; remains staged until confirmed. Ambulance Unit 417 follows instructions, asks clarification, reports facility arrival and patient handover complete. Fleet Maintenance Cell Bluejay provides unavailable/restricted vehicle info and Battery Swap Voucher. North Gate Status Board provides Queue Snapshot; South Gate Status Board displays southern access and produces South Access Lane Notice for material south-approach constraint. Hospital Liaison Desk Kestrel provides capacity/contact/constraints, coordinates ED consultation, communicates restrictions, produces Bedside Arrival Receipt, remains available for handover questions, uses Pediatric Acuity Note for pediatric monitoring/destination considerations. Emergency Department (ED) advises capacity/access/receiving status and clarifies patient identity/transfer documentation with crew before clearing. Shift Commander Sundial approves exceptions, reviews access/surge coverage, assigns coordination, escalates unresolved destination/access issues, sends Mutual Aid Release Form. Triage Supervisor validates surge/prioritization. Regional Medical Director sets priorities and directs demand/protocol adjustments. Call Taker Mara receives Bedside Arrival Receipt and verifies arrival time vs timeline/comms. Data Quality Officer reviews/corrects inconsistent/incomplete

New part:
S181: Call Taker Mara obtains the age, weight when available, and caregiver observations needed to support pediatric triage.
S182: Paramedic Crew reassesses pediatric patients during transport and reports material changes to the receiving facility.
S183: Kestrel shall confirm that facility capacity and pediatric service limitations are communicated to dispatch before a destination is finalized.
S184: Riverside Trauma Center advises Hospital Liaison Desk when trauma intake conditions may affect the suitability of an otherwise appropriate destination.
S185: Emergency Department staff acknowledge destination changes through the established coordination channel and identify any immediate access restrictions.
S186: Hospital Liaison Desk records facility responses in the regional coordination record and keeps dispatch informed of unresolved constraints.
S187: Mutual aid is requested when local staffed units cannot meet the declared response objectives or when a specialized resource is unavailable.
S188: Regional Radio Network carries mutual-aid requests, acceptance confirmations, and operational updates using the agreed regional call signs.
S189: Copperfield shall approve any temporary triage override and document its rationale before the override is applied.
S190: Ambulance Coordination Platform tracks accepted mutual-aid assignments separately from locally staffed resources to preserve an accurate coverage view.
S191: Ambulance Unit 417 may be reassigned only after dispatch confirms that its current patient-care and transport obligations permit the change.
S192: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports a vehicle restriction promptly so dispatch does not count an unavailable unit toward operational coverage.
S193: Triage Supervisor reviews the audit memo before closing a suspected duplicate incident.
S194: Data Quality Officer reviews unresolved record discrepancies through the established quality process without delaying active patient care.
S195: North Gate Status Board provides a current view of access conditions that may affect ambulance approach or handover timing.
S196: South Gate Status Board provides the equivalent access view for routes and entry points on the southern side of the region.
S197: After surge conditions ease, Shift Commander confirms that outstanding assignments, destination constraints, and staffing gaps have been handed over to the next operational period.
S198: Regional Dispatch Center maintains a degraded-radio procedure that prioritizes emergency traffic and preserves a common operating picture.
S199: Regional Radio Network operators announce channel outages, affected areas, and expected restoration times over the remaining service channels.
S200: Radio Coordinator directs crews to approved fallback channels when the primary channel is unusable.
S201: Crews acknowledge each fallback assignment and repeat critical location and destination details before moving.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
